trust_decision.summary: CSV cell values from an uploaded import file (untrusted, authenticated user) are treated as SQL data when the injection library looks up existing items/users/contacts/templates; decided (or not) at each raw-SQL lookup in inc/commoninjectionlib.class.php and per-itemtype injection classes. NOTE: the listed fix commit is a pure version bump (fix.diff:5-43, CHANGELOG/xml/setup.php only); the actual escaping change appears to be the pinned commit itself ('fix/ escape SQL values (#627)', CHANGELOG.md:8-12), which already uses $DB->request with an array WHERE in dataAlreadyInDB.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'SQL injection via CSV import'; the generic injection library's existence check (dataAlreadyInDB) is the central DB lookup of CSV values, and the pinned-tree regression test targets it (tests/unit/CommonInjectionLibDataAlreadyInDbTest.php:43-45).

fix_sites.entry_point: none - fix diff changes only version strings (setup.php, datainjection.xml, CHANGELOG.md); no source fix site

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Per-itemtype lookups (software name, network port name/MAC) live in itemtype-specific classes outside the generic library the report points at, and can be argued as 'only used when that model type is chosen'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Name values containing apostrophes/accents (e.g. O'Brien) must still match existing records; an over-broad fix that strips or rejects quotes breaks matching.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a checkPresent() extra condition built as a raw string by an itemtype class
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the library still tolerates/warns on non-array checkPresent returns (inc/commoninjectionlib.class.php:1992-2000), so an itemtype class returning a string fragment is plausible legacy code

O9_family: SQL injection (CWE-89), string-concatenated raw queries with CSV values
